DataPropertyAssertion.Literal: Control ontology for the DL corner cases (consistency tests). Each expectation derived from the DL semantics. . Note: usesOntology is a relative file name in the same directory. Run configurations (kt:usesTestRunConfig) and reasoner configurations (kt:usesTestSystemConfig) may be assigned to the suite and apply to all of its tests.
Per test: ClassAssertion(ConsistencyTest) + task + usesOntology + expectedResult
A data max cardinality of one on xsd:dateTimeStamp is consistent with a single value of the datatype.
Two distinct xsd:dateTimeStamp values violate a data max cardinality of one.
An existential restriction whose successor is an inverse-at-most witness: satisfying it requires merging the named individual with another successor, which the saturation must not decide on its own.
The same contradiction behind a class definition (the asserted concept does not reveal it).
Margherita is subsumed by VegetarianPizza through the all-values restriction.

Issue #19: three pigeons on two holes force one hole to hold two pigeons, so the scene of that hole is a CrowdedScene and Scene is subsumed by CrowdedScene. This is the classifier's own test concept (Scene and not CrowdedScene) and it must be unsatisfiable.

Negative control for the pigeonhole case: the scene itself is a CrowdedScene, so (Scene and CrowdedScene) must stay satisfiable. A fix for the missing subsumption must not make this class unsatisfiable.

Issue #19, reduced variant from the issue discussion: one hole, two pigeons and the redundant axiom CrowdedHole subsumed by Hole. Removing that axiom makes the answer correct, so it belongs to the reproduction; the test concept must be unsatisfiable.
Negative control for the reduced pigeonhole variant: (Scene and CrowdedScene) must stay satisfiable.

Issue #19 as an ABox test: the ontology entails CrowdedScene(s), so asserting its negation must make the knowledge base inconsistent. This case passes and guards the ABox path while the cached subsumption test is repaired.
Issue #19 as reported: the classification must place Scene and CrowdedScene in one equivalence class (and TestSceneNotCrowded under owl:Nothing).
Issue #19, reduced variant: Scene and CrowdedScene must be classified as equivalent.

Nominal merge edge case: Node is the nominal {n}, k is an r-predecessor of n and a Forbidden, so (Node and (inverse r only (not Forbidden))) is inconsistent. The universal restriction is expanded on the test node before the merge with the nominal moves the link of k onto it, so the merge has to apply the restriction to the moved neighbour as well.

Negative control for the nominal merge edge case: the same universal restriction with the compatible filler Marker must stay satisfiable, so a fix for the missing application to the merged neighbours must not over-constrain them.

The existential counterpart of the nominal merge edge case: (Node and (inverse r some Forbidden)) is satisfiable and, because k is an r-predecessor of n, equivalent to Node, so the entailment Node is subsumed by (inverse r some Forbidden) is checked by the classification test of the same ontology.

Classification of the nominal merge edge case: TestForallMerge must be placed under owl:Nothing, TestForallMergeOk under Node, and Node and TestExistsMerge must be equivalent (the merge moves the predecessor link of k onto the nominal).

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is unsatisfiable. The test merges the scene nominal into the test node, so the nodes that the cached model merged into the holes have to be rebuilt (criteria C8 and C11).
Control for the issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (the holes are linked to the scene by role assertions): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene and CrowdedScene are equivalent.

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is unsatisfiable. The test merges the scene nominal into the test node, so the nodes that the cached model merged into the holes have to be rebuilt (criteria C8 and C11).
Control for the issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (four pigeons on three holes, so three merged hole successors per model): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene and CrowdedScene are equivalent.

Completion graph caching, issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): (Scene and not CrowdedScene) is satisfiable. The rebuilt part of the cached model must not produce a clash that the knowledge base does not entail.
Control for the issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): (Scene and CrowdedScene) is satisfiable.

Classification of the issue #19 variant (negative control, two pigeons on two holes need not share a hole): runs many satisfiability tests on the same cached completion graph, Scene is not subsumed by CrowdedScene.
